headline: Seven unpatched FatFs flaws expose millions of embedded devices as extortionists skip encryption and cheap Telegram gigs harvest selfie videos for fraud.

emerging_trends.text: Widely embedded code keeps turning into wide exposure, as runZero's seven unpatched FatFs flaws sit inside the firmware of security cameras, drones, industrial controllers, and hardware crypto wallets that ship without an easy fix.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Seven Unpatched FatFs Flaws Threaten Embedded Devices

emerging_trends.text: Extortion crews increasingly abandon the encryptor, as the Kairos group pried $1 million from a U.S. government entity purely by threatening to leak stolen files.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Kairos Extorts U.S. Government Entity for $1 Million

emerging_trends.text: Cheap online gigs now hunt for faces, with a $7 Face Motion Video Project on Telegram recruiting people to hand over selfie videos that likely feed deepfake fraud.

topics.title: $7 Telegram Gig Harvests Selfie Videos
topics.latest_developments: Frank McKenna's Frank on Fraud flagged on July 5 a Telegram recruiting ad called the Face Motion Video Project that pays $7 for a few minutes of work uploading selfie videos, footage he suspects feeds fraud.
topics.summary: The advertisement offers recruits $7 to hand over short selfie videos of themselves, material that could feed deepfake creation or identity-verification fraud; job seekers should treat any selfie-for-pay gig as a warning sign.

sources.title: Super Sketchy $7 Gig Recruits People To Send Selfie Videos

topics.title: Kairos Extorts U.S. Government Entity for $1 Million
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News on July 4 published Rakesh Krishnan's Ransom-ISAC reconstruction, built from a leaked negotiation chat and the blockchain trail the payment left, showing Kairos took the money without locking a single file and may not be a ransomware gang at all.
topics.summary: Kairos ran pure data-theft extortion against an unnamed U.S. government entity, threatening to leak stolen files unless it paid; the case shows extortion crews increasingly drop encryption and rely on leak threats alone.

sources.title: U.S. Government Entity Paid Kairos $1 Million in Data-Theft Extortion Case

topics.title: Seven Unpatched FatFs Flaws Threaten Embedded Devices
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News on July 3 laid out runZero's seven still-unpatched FatFs flaws by device class, naming the security cameras, drones, industrial controllers, and hardware crypto wallets whose firmware reads FAT and exFAT USB drives and SD cards through the library.
topics.summary: FatFs is a small filesystem library embedded in the firmware of millions of devices, and runZero found seven vulnerabilities that carry no fix; device makers must watch for vendor patches and restrict untrusted removable media.

sources.title: Unpatched Flaws Disclosed in Filesystem Bundled Into Millions of Embedded Devices

business_politics.title: NATO Leaders Convene in Ankara
business_politics.latest_developments: NATO's heads of state opened a summit in Ankara on July 5 centered on whether members can turn pledged spending increases into actual weapons, with a signaled U.S. troop drawdown from Europe hanging over the talks.
business_politics.summary: Secretary-general Mark Rutte pressed the alliance to convert swelling defense budgets into munitions, warning that contractors are straining to keep pace with orders, as an American move to pull forces from the continent rattled allies watching Vladimir Putin's Russia.

sources.title: Nato leaders gather for crucial meeting in Ankara
NATO Is Fixing Its Cash Flow Problem. Now It Needs to Turn Money Into Munitions.

business_politics.title: Burnham Set to Take Over Number 10
business_politics.latest_developments: Nominations opened July 5 in Labour's leadership contest, positioning Andy Burnham to succeed Keir Starmer as UK prime minister as soon as July 20.
business_politics.summary: Andy Burnham, the mayor of Greater Manchester, is on course to enter Downing Street within weeks even as allies warn he has yet to form a cabinet, while the SNP and English regions press him over how far he will devolve power.

sources.title: Burnham warned over lack of cabinet as Number 10 transition talks step up
Burnham faces tricky electoral test as Starmer pushes through local government shake-up

business.title: Binko's Hot Sauce Draws Crowds at Giant Eagle
business.latest_developments: Binko's Pymatuning Lake Chili Co., a Pittsburgh hot-sauce maker, ran a tasting during last week's heat wave at the Giant Eagle Market District store at The Waterworks.
business.summary: Shoppers sampled Binko's Coolhand Habanero Pepper Sauce at the Market District tasting, a small-batch western Pennsylvania company working its way onto the grocer's shelves.

sources.title: Dig in With Graver: Turning up the Heat at Giant Eagle

business.title: Pitt Video Game Sharpens ER Trauma Care
business.latest_developments: A University of Pittsburgh study found that a video game a Pittsburgh physician built measurably improved emergency-room doctors' treatment decisions for older trauma patients.
business.summary: The Pitt research reported that the game prompted peers to reconsider how they treat elderly trauma cases and produced better calls, an early validation of game-based clinical training.

sources.title: University of Pittsburgh study finds video game improves ER doctors' decisions for older trauma patients

around_town.title: Flood Watch Follows the Heat Wave
around_town.latest_developments: The National Weather Service placed most of western Pennsylvania under a flood watch from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m. Sunday, July 5, as the multi-day heat wave broke and heavy rain returned.
around_town.summary: After the region's fifth 90-degree day, storms dropped more rain on ground already soaked over the holiday weekend, making flash flooding the chief hazard across greater Pittsburgh even as Saturday's damaging winds eased.

sources.title: Flood Watch to go into effect for most of Western Pa.
Pittsburgh region under flood watch as chance for storms returns through the evening

around_town.title: Parkway East Closure Primer Airs
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE's '4 The Record' sat down with a PennDOT executive this week to walk drivers through the 25-day Parkway East closure that begins at 9 p.m. July 10.
around_town.summary: PennDOT will shut the Parkway East between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and the Edgewood/Swissvale exit to replace the aging Commercial Street Bridge near Frick Park, a detour the agency urges commuters to plan around now.

sources.title: 'Scheduling is everything': '4 The Record' gets you ready for the closure of part of the Parkway East

events.title: Taste of Picklesburgh Opens Downtown
events.latest_developments: The Taste of Picklesburgh begins Thursday, July 9, with downtown Pittsburgh restaurants and businesses rolling out pickle-inspired specials ahead of the main festival.
events.summary: Picklesburgh, the nationally recognized food festival celebrating all things briny and dill, returns to downtown Pittsburgh, and participating downtown eateries kick it off July 9 with pickle-themed dishes and drinks.

sources.title: Downtown Pittsburgh businesses to offer pickle-inspired specials ahead of Picklesburgh

around_teams.title: Carter Fields Steelers Offseason Questions
around_teams.latest_developments: In a July 2 live chat, Post-Gazette Steelers writer Christopher Carter took reader questions on quarterback Aaron Rodgers, receiver DK Metcalf, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. ahead of training camp.
around_teams.summary: Carter's chat gauged Pittsburgh's 2026 outlook, weighing Rodgers's fit under center, Metcalf's role in the passing game, and the still-unresolved contract situation of Joey Porter Jr. as the team prepares to report to Saint Vincent College.

around_teams.title: Hiles Spreads the Blame for Skenes
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles published a July 3 deep dive parsing who bears responsibility for ace Paul Skenes's slump.
around_teams.summary: Hiles spread the fault across the Pirates' pitch-calling and coaching after Skenes surrendered a career-high eight runs to the Phillies, arguing the breakdown reaches past the pitcher to his catchers and staff.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: Who's to blame for Paul Skenes' struggles? A deep dive reveals plenty of possibilities

team_usa.title: Balogun Cleared to Face Belgium
team_usa.latest_developments: FIFA's disciplinary committee suspended Folarin Balogun's red-card ban on July 5, clearing the U.S. striker to play Monday's round-of-16 match against Belgium after the White House lobbied FIFA to reverse it.
team_usa.summary: Balogun, the Americans' leading scorer with three goals, drew a red card for stepping on Bosnia and Herzegovina's Tarik Muharemović in a 2-0 last-32 win, and his reinstatement, which the Belgian federation called astonishing, restores the U.S. attack to full strength in Seattle.

sources.title: FIFA suspends Balogun red card, can face Belgium
White House lobbied Fifa to lift Folarin Balogun suspension for World Cup game v Belgium

team_usa.title: Ream Calls the Squad America's Mirror
team_usa.latest_developments: Ahead of Monday's Belgium match, USMNT captain Tim Ream called the roster 'a true representation of what America is,' spotlighting its diverse backgrounds.
team_usa.summary: Defender Tim Ream, reflecting on the co-hosts' run to the round of 16, framed the team's mix of backgrounds as emblematic of the country as the United States readies for Belgium in Seattle.

sources.title: Ream: USMNT a 'true representation of America'

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: The AI Industry Is Losing
reading.summary: Zitron marshals financials from NVIDIA, Anthropic, and OpenAI to argue the AI industry is bleeding money and losing the narrative, contending the build-out's economics simply do not add up.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Beware of Productivity Paradoxes
reading.summary: Newport uses the personal computer's uneven productivity record to warn that a technology poised to be an obvious efficiency win can disappoint, a caution he extends to today's assumptions about AI.

reading.title: An Interview with Figma CEO Dylan Field About Design and AI
reading.summary: Ben Thompson interviews Figma chief executive Dylan Field on how he built the design company and why he believes AI works as a tailwind rather than a threat to its business.
